- When sentiment is negative in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen forecast slope downward in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive, model tends to overestimate future prices — apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecast mean.
- Model underestimates when sentiment shifts from positive to negative — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for sentiment reversal.
- Forecast horizon 30d often shows lag: model reacts to sentiment 1–2 days after it changes — delay correction by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overforecast — apply conservative correction (−1.5% to −3%) to avoid overconfidence bias.
